newsitem.title: TURKEY: Seven firms interested in Turkish aluminium plant.
newsitem.headline: Seven firms interested in Turkish aluminium plant.

text.p: Seven international and local companies have shown interest in a Turkish government tender to upgrade the capacity and production technology of its sole primary aluminium smelter, a senior official said on Tuesday.
"The seven companies which received tender terms are to submit their bids by August 26," said Ismet Sivrioglu, deputy general manager of state mining company Etibank.

The companies which took tender terms are Glencore International, Raytheon Engineering, a unit of U.S. Raytheon Co, Daewoo Corp, ICF Kaiser International Inc, Billiton International Metals BV, a unit of South African Gencor Ltd, Turkey's Koc Holding AS and Doruk Proje.

"The companies' bids will include the method of production to be used at the Seydisehir aluminium smelter, the new production capacity for primary aluminium and the method of power supplies," Sivrioglu told Reuters.

The project, estimated to cost around $315 million, envisages a rise in annual capacity at Seydisehir to 100,000-200,000 tonnes of primary aluminium from 60,000 and a change in technology from the Russian-designed Soderberg system.
The winner should also improve power supply to the smelter, located in southern Turkey, either through a new nearby power plant that it will build or from the national power grid.
Etibank put out the tender in April.
According to the tender terms, Etibank, which wholly owns the plant, will form a joint partnership with the winner of the tender and have a stake between 15 and 49 percent.
Sivrioglu said Etibank's contribution to the capital of the partnership would be made from its assets at the existing plant.
The project has an investment period of four years and is expected to pay off the cost in five years.
